I know that you can do better
than that.

title.label: Perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock

content.label:
I’ve found Due to be the perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock. By keeping only time-sensitive reminders, it ensures you’re not overloaded with notifications or becoming desensitized to them—something that can happen with other reminder apps. Due keeps you accountable without being overwhelming.

Beyond the app itself, the customer service is exceptional. I reached out three times with specific questions, and each time, I received thoughtful responses—either the same day or the next—along with personalized recommendations on how to make the most of the app. That level of support is rare and truly appreciated.

The only thing to be mindful of when importing reminders from Apple’s Reminders app is that Due automatically marks them as completed in the original app. However, there’s a simple workaround: instead of importing everything at once, you can hand-pick specific reminders to be imported without Due marking them as complete in iOS Reminders. To do this, turn on a setting named ‘Show in Side Menu’ under Due > Settings, in a section called System Reminders near the bottom. This lets you manually select reminders before they are added to Due.

I did a lot of research before choosing Due, and I’m happy to say it works well for me. But even if it hadn’t, I can see how it would still be a great fit for many people. It has plenty of features and customization options, making it versatile enough to suit different needs and workflows. If you’re looking for a powerful yet simple reminder system, Due is definitely worth considering. 

Overall, Due is a fantastic tool for anyone who wants an effective, no-fuss reminder system that actually helps you stay on top of tasks without bombarding you with notifications. Highly recommend!
